# Failoverly

> Failoverly is an automatic internet failover app for macOS. It uses an iPhone connected over USB with Personal Hotspot as backup internet to preserve online sessions during outages and sudden slowdowns.

Official website: https://failoverly.app/. The landing page is the primary source for product details.

- Status: prelaunch. Visitors can join the email waitlist through an embedded Kit form to receive the launch announcement. Joining does not purchase the app or start a paid subscription.
- Planned subscription: US$6.99 per month for the US and Canada. Early registrants are offered their first month free when the product launches.
- Platform: macOS only.
- Requirements: a Mac, a primary internet connection, and an iPhone connected over USB with Personal Hotspot enabled, cellular coverage, and a compatible data plan. Android and wireless backup connections are not supported at launch.
- Failoverly monitors latency and packet loss. It can use the backup when the primary connection drops or becomes unreliable even while Wi-Fi remains connected, then automatically switches back when it recovers to save cellular data.
- Traffic uses an encrypted VPN tunnel to Failoverly-operated servers. This preserves the service-facing connection while the Mac changes its local network connection. A brief pause during the switch is possible.
- The VPN can add latency and change the apparent location seen by online services. Its purpose is connection stability; it does not guarantee lower ping.
- Failoverly does not repair Wi-Fi, combine connection speeds, speed up the internet, or guarantee lower ping. It cannot keep sessions online if both connections fail or resolve an outage of the destination service itself.
- Typical uses: work calls, online coaching, webinars, live streaming, online games, SSH/remote development, and trading platforms.

## Product and setup

- [Landing page](https://failoverly.app/): product overview, requirements, planned pricing, and FAQ.
- [How it works](https://failoverly.app/#how-it-works): backup setup, connection monitoring, encrypted tunnel, and return to the primary connection.

## Questions and limitations

- [FAQ](https://failoverly.app/#faq): session continuity, cellular data use, channel bonding, and Mac hotspot behavior.
